topic: Sneezing: reflex, heart myth, droplet distance, photic sneeze, holding it in
hook: What happens to your body when you sneeze
caption:
A sneeze is a reflex your brainstem fires. MIT researchers filmed sneeze clouds carrying droplets up to 8 meters across a room.

And holding one in is a bad idea. In 2018, doctors in the UK described a man who tore his throat after pinching his nose and closing his mouth mid-sneeze (BMJ Case Reports).

Be honest: do you sneeze when you look at the sun? 👇

🎨 AI-generated image

1/5 It starts in your nose
Irritants hit nerve endings in your nose. A signal races to your brainstem, which fires the sneeze reflex.
📷 unknown (CC0 / public domain) via openverse

2/5 Your heart doesn't stop (Myth)
Pure myth. Chest pressure can briefly change your heart rhythm, but your heart keeps beating the whole time.
📷 Dguendel (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

3/5 The cloud travels far (8 m)
MIT researchers filmed sneeze clouds carrying droplets up to 8 meters across a room.
📷 Metacladistics (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

4/5 Bright light can trigger it (1 in 4)
The photic sneeze reflex makes roughly 1 in 4 people sneeze when they step into bright sunlight.
🎨 AI-generated image

5/5 Never hold one in (2018)
In 2018, doctors reported a man who tore his throat holding in a sneeze with his nose and mouth shut.
